## The splash tells you what you're running, and the main screen stops overcounting

A small follow-up to v1.4.0. If you're coming from anything older than that, v1.4.0 is the one you actually want -- it fixed a real crash-on-commute bug where NimBLE quietly retained every distinct BLE address it had ever seen. This release just tidies two things on top of it.

The boot splash now prints the firmware version next to `INITIALIZING...`, so "which build is this device on?" is answerable by watching it start up instead of by guessing from which features are present. It's stamped from `git describe` at build time, which means it's the real tag rather than a number someone remembered to bump.

The main screen's header also stops saying something slightly untrue. It read `DETECTIONS LOGGED`, but the number beside it isn't a log count -- entries age out and decrement it, so it's a count of what's currently active, and it would tick back down while the log itself still held every one of those rows. It now reads `ACTIVE DETECTIONS`, which is what it was measuring the whole time.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: the firmware version on the boot splash, appended to the `INITIALIZING...` line and stamped from `git describe` at build time
- **Changed**: the main screen's `DETECTIONS LOGGED` header is now `ACTIVE DETECTIONS` -- the count it sits next to decrements as detections go stale, so it was never a log total
